full_caption: Amberline Property Group, Inc., Appellant, v. Kingsmere Homeowners Association, Inc., Appellee
fictional_notice: FICTIONAL DOCUMENT. Generated for the LegalCase Responder demo corpus. The parties, court, docket number and holdings below are invented and do not correspond to any real case, court, or person.

sections.heading: Paragraph 1
sections.text: Appellant Amberline Property Group, Inc. is the record owner of the residential building located at 2631 Harper's Cut, Elmsworth, AR, a 12-unit structure operated as rental housing since 1980. Appellee Kingsmere Homeowners Association, Inc. occupied Unit 3A under a written lease dated June 26, 2003.

sections.heading: Paragraph 2
sections.text: The record establishes that Amberline Property Group, Inc. received written notice of the heating defect on October 10, 2002 and did not dispatch a repair contractor until June 27, 2008, an interval of 21 days. During that interval overnight interior temperatures fell below fifty-five degrees on at least eleven occasions.

sections.heading: Paragraph 3
sections.text: The lease provided for monthly rent of $1,875, due on the first day of each month, with a late charge of $50 assessed on any installment remaining unpaid after the 3th day of the month. The trial court found that this charge operated as a penalty rather than as liquidated damages.

sections.heading: Paragraph 4
sections.text: Kingsmere Homeowners Association, Inc. withheld rent for the months of May and November of 1987, asserting that the premises were untenantable by reason of a persistent failure of the heating system and recurring water intrusion at the north wall of the unit.

sections.heading: Paragraph 5
sections.text: The trial court awarded Kingsmere Homeowners Association, Inc. attorney's fees of $13,000 under the reciprocal-fee provision. Where a lease grants fees to the landlord, this State reads the provision as mutual, and the prevailing tenant recovers on the same terms.

sections.heading: Paragraph 6
sections.text: The security deposit of $3,600 was not returned within 30 days of surrender, nor was an itemized statement of deductions furnished. The statutory consequence is forfeiture of the landlord's right to retain any portion of the deposit.

sections.heading: Paragraph 7
sections.text: A late fee is enforceable only where it bears a reasonable relationship to the administrative cost actually incurred by the landlord in processing a delinquent payment. A charge of $50 against a monthly obligation of $1,875 exceeds that relationship and is unenforceable to the extent it exceeds five percent of the installment.

sections.heading: Paragraph 8
sections.text: Retaliatory eviction is presumed where a landlord commences a summary possession action within 12 months after a tenant has reported a code violation to the municipal housing inspector. The presumption is rebuttable by clear and convincing evidence of an independent, non-retaliatory ground.

sections.heading: Paragraph 9
sections.text: A tenant electing to withhold rent under the repair-and-deduct statute must (1) give written notice of the defect, (2) allow a reasonable time for cure, and (3) deposit the withheld sums with the clerk of court or into a segregated account. Kingsmere Homeowners Association, Inc. satisfied the first two requirements but did not deposit the withheld rent.

sections.heading: Paragraph 10
sections.text: The implied warranty of habitability is not waivable by lease term. Any provision purporting to require a tenant to accept the premises 'as is' is void as against the public policy of this State insofar as it reaches conditions materially affecting health and safety.

sections.heading: Paragraph 11
sections.text: We affirm in part and reverse in part. The judgment of possession is vacated; the money judgment is remanded for recalculation consistent with the late-fee holding set out above.

sections.heading: RIDER C — SECURITY DEPOSIT
sections.text: Landlord holds the sum of $3,600 as security for Tenant's performance. The deposit shall be held in a segregated interest-bearing account at a federally insured institution located within this State. Within 30 days after surrender of the Premises, Landlord shall return the deposit together with accrued interest, less any lawful deductions, accompanied by an itemized written statement identifying each deduction and attaching supporting invoices. Failure to furnish the itemized statement within that period forfeits Landlord's right to retain any portion of the deposit.

sections.heading: RIDER D — PETS AND ASSISTANCE ANIMALS
sections.text: No animal shall be kept on the Premises without Landlord's prior written consent, except that this Rider does not apply to a service animal or to a reasonable accommodation required by fair-housing law, for which no pet deposit or pet rent may be charged. Where consent is granted, Tenant shall pay a refundable pet deposit of $250 and shall be liable for all damage caused by the animal beyond ordinary wear.

sections.heading: RIDER E — SUBLETTING AND EARLY TERMINATION
sections.text: Tenant may not sublet the Premises or assign this Lease without Landlord's written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed. Tenant may terminate early upon 30 days' written notice and payment of a termination fee equal to two (2) monthly installments, provided that no termination fee shall be charged where the termination follows Landlord's material breach, a lawful lease-break for domestic violence, or military relocation orders.

sections.heading: Clause 1 — Inspection and Right of Entry
sections.text: Upon not less than twenty-four (24) hours' prior notice, and at reasonable times, a party may enter upon the subject premises to inspect, to make permitted repairs, or to show the premises to a prospective purchaser or lender. Entry without notice is permitted only in an emergency threatening life or substantial property damage, and the entering party shall give notice of the entry as soon as practicable thereafter.

sections.heading: Clause 2 — Insurance
sections.text: The party in possession shall maintain commercial general liability insurance of not less than $2,000,000 per occurrence, naming the other party as an additional insured, and shall furnish a certificate of insurance on request and on each renewal. Each party waives subrogation against the other to the extent of insurance proceeds actually received.

sections.heading: Clause 3 — Counterparts and Electronic Signature
sections.text: This instrument may be executed in counterparts, each of which is an original and all of which together constitute one instrument. A signature delivered electronically has the same effect as an original, provided that any instrument submitted for recording shall bear original signatures and acknowledgment before a notary public of the State of Ardenne.
